subject: Monthly commit & step-up ramp — clarifying pricing and flexibility
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex@luminari.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@luminari.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify monthly ramp schedule for hosted API commit

Connor —

Thanks for the call earlier. We're excited to move forward but need to lock down how the monthly commit and step-up schedule would work for our launch timeline. A few specifics from our side:

- Expected baseline usage during beta (Jul): ~250M tokens / month.
- Launch month (Aug): spike to ~1.1B tokens.
- Post-launch steady state (Sep onward): ~600–700M tokens, with seasonal spikes (Nov/Dec) up to ~1.4B.

Our questions:
1) Can Redwood structure a monthly commit that steps up (e.g., 250M in Jul -> 600M in Sep -> 1.0B by Nov) while preserving per-token discounted pricing at each step?
2) How do unused committed tokens roll forward? We need clarity on quarter rollover vs. monthly forfeiture.
3) Is there an option for a mid-quarter adjustment (we expect some volatility and want to avoid paying full overage at list rate right after a launch spike)?

Also, we have legal & finance asking about credits for unused commit in Q1 if the ramp is pushed by marketing — any precedent?

Would appreciate a short written proposal we can show finance. Happy to sync with marissa or rishi if you want product/usage context.

Best,
Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Partnerships | Luminari Games
---
Attachment: product_roadmap_v2.pdf (ref)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@luminari.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify monthly ramp schedule for hosted API commit

Alex —

Thanks for the clear numbers. I've sketched three practical approaches and attached a spreadsheet that lays out token counts and monthly cost examples (commit_schedule_proposal.xlsx) plus our standard pricing grid (redwood-pricing-grid.pdf). High level:

Option A — Conservative step-up (recommended for predictable finance):
- Jul: 250M committed tokens
- Aug: 600M committed tokens
- Sep+: 700M committed tokens with pre-agreed step-ups to 1.0B in Nov if MAU thresholds are met
- Discounts applied at each committed tier (sliding per-token rate). Unused tokens: quarter-level rollover (up to 30% cap) or conversion to credits at 50% list for excess credits beyond cap.

Option B — Aggressive launch-first (minimize overage risk at launch):
- Jul: 400M commit, Aug: 1.0B commit, Sep: 700M commit
- Built-in one-time buffer for launch month; any unused buffer can be converted to credits valid for 60 days.

Option C — Monthly flexible commit with ramp guardrails:
- Month-to-month commits with a pre-approved step-up window (3 business days notice) to avoid punitive overage. Higher per-token discount only for locked step-ups of 2+ months.

Other notes:
- Overage pricing: list per-token rate with a blended cap if step-up request is made within 14 days post-billing period.
- Mid-quarter adjustments: we can provide an "adjustment credit" for one mid-quarter change per contract year (subject to mapping usage to MAU).
- Early termination / launch delay: custom credit handling is negotiable for enterprise deals (we've done partial crediting for customers who delayed launches due to marketing).

Next steps: if you prefer Option A or B we'll produce a redline-friendly term sheet and provide sample month-by-month invoices in the Drive link. Can we set 30 minutes tomorrow to review?

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Thu, Jun 4, 2026 at 9:05 AM Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex —
> 
> Thanks for the clear numbers. I've sketched three practical approaches and attached a spreadsheet...

Connor —

Appreciate the quick options. A couple of follow-ups so we can get finance comfortable:

- For Option A: the quarter-level rollover with a 30% cap — does that apply per month (i.e., each month's unused can be rolled) or aggregate for the whole quarter?
- Can we get a mechanism where the first post-launch month (Aug) overage is billed at a blended rate (e.g., 60% list) if we triggered an unplanned spike and request step-up within 10 days? That would reduce our immediate cashflow stress.
- If we pick Option B (aggressive), what's the minimum notice to adjust downward if launch is postponed? Finance won't sign for a large locked commit without some downward adjustment path.

Also want to propose a hybrid: Jul commit 250M, Aug buffer 400M (buffer priced at 70% of the committed discounted rate), Sep onward 700M. That keeps initial cash outlay lower but gives breathing room at launch. Would Redwood consider converting any unused buffer to a service credit applied to observability add-ons?

If you can update the spreadsheet with the hybrid numbers and a sample invoice for Aug showing blended billing, that would be perfect. Priya and I can then aim to get this to procurement by Monday.

Best,
Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Partnerships | Luminari Games

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@luminari.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify monthly ramp schedule for hosted API commit

Alex —

Great — I'll update the attached spreadsheet with the hybrid scenario (250M base + 400M buffer at 70% discount example) and include a sample blended invoice for Aug. Quick answers inline:

- Rollover: the 30% cap is applied at the quarter aggregate level (unused from any month in the quarter can be pooled up to 30% of the quarter's committed total). We'll call that out in the term sheet explicitly.
- Blended overage: we can support a one-time blended overage of 60% list for a post-launch spike if a step-up is requested within 10 days — we'll include language for a single-use grace per launch event.
- Downward adjustment for Option B: 30 days notice for a one-time downward adjustment with a 15% administrative fee on the difference; we can soften that for strategic partners in the final redline.

I'll share the revised spreadsheet and a short draft term sheet by end of day. If it looks good, let's lock a 30-minute sign-off with procurement on Monday (I'll send a calendar invite).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
